summary.text: One stipulated 300 rpm trial stopped at second 60 and yielded vial attenuations 0.204, 0.209, 0.207, approximately 2.4 percent spread. This bounded counterexample challenges universal necessity of sustained 900 rpm and optical stability. Reliable lower-speed sufficiency, syringe success and the optical return loop remain hypotheses.

Stage1 migration hypothesis: replace rotation with six needle-free 20 mL low-position withdrawals and upper-side returns, completed at ten-second marks through second 60. Keep the stirrer off; stop transfers independently of images. Predicted second-120 depth-vial spread is at most 4 percent; success remains unobserved.

Distinct second attack removes the migrated carrier: zero transfers and zero stirring before identical sampling. Hypothesis A predicts migration passes and this attack fails. Rival hypothesis B predicts both pass through passive redistribution or sampling-mediated equalization. Replicated separation supports carrier contribution within this recipe, without proving unique necessity.

Use six fresh trials as two triplets: fixed 300 rpm for 60 seconds, syringe migration, zero-transfer attack. Reverse arm order in triplet two; fix addition location, bottle and locked camera. Active operations end at second 60, matching quiet intervals. Sample three depths from second 120 within ten seconds; alternate sampling order. Use common references, log optical checks without feedback, and report readings, durations, transfers and failures. Use spill tray; stop if liquid escapes.

residue.text: Source-bound shared concern retained outside the six-trial construction: INV proposes enabled versus fixed-duration 900 rpm and matched 300/900 rpm or brief stir-off comparisons. Hypothesis: agitation-generated image disturbance triggers further agitation; rival: gradients warrant further mixing. These comparisons are unperformed, would require another session, and cannot identify bubbles. Different cessation times also confound final samples through differing quiet intervals.

ATT proposes repeated fixed 300 rpm, 60-second trials with no optical restart; the retained reference arm partially incorporates that concern. Repeat success and time savings are unknown: preferred total duration and matched 900 rpm final vials are absent. Sampling order can affect readings; commanded rpm lacks independent verification.

Stage1 unresolved residue: migration failure leaves transfer dose unresolved; both arms passing cannot distinguish passive transport from sampling disturbance. Limited replication and order effects constrain inference. Specks remain unidentified, reference repeatability is not calibration, and bubble fraction and absolute concentration are unmeasurable. Other recipes, vessels and continuous processes remain untested; this synthetic proxy establishes no real chemical or human benefit.
